correctness.rationale: Geodesic intervals in P_m x P_n are Cartesian coordinate intervals, so every nonempty geodesically convex vertex set is a grid rectangle, with empty set allowed. For each support S (size>=2), every subset is a rectangle trace iff each point p lies outside the bounding rectangle of S\{p}, equivalent to being a unique strict minimum or maximum along some coordinate. Therefore |S|<=4. A nonshattered triple has a unique point between the other two in both coordinates; summing weak-quadrant inclusion–exclusion over all lattice points gives cubic coefficient mn(m-1)(n-1)(2mn-m-n-4)/18. Shattered quadruples biject with four distinct extreme labels and have quartic coefficient m(m-1)^2(m-2)n(n-1)^2(n-2)/144. Constant, linear, quadratic coefficients are 1,mn,binom(mn,2); no higher coefficients. Boundary VC dimensions are 1 (1x1), 2 (path or 2x2), 3 (2xn,n>2), 4 (both>=3). As both dimensions grow random triple/quad shattering probabilities tend 2/3 and 1/6. Source grid_shattering_check.py all-rectangle trace enumeration was inspected; independent combinatorial spot checks agree, but infinite formulas follow algebraic counting.
